note: Matomo Reports displays reports from an external Matomo server. Its connection settings live in the simple config object matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings (keys matomo_server_url, matomo_reports_token_auth, matomo_reports_allowed_sites, matomo_server_url_ignore_ssl); the settings form is /admin/config/system/matomo-reports (route matomo_reports.matomo_reports_settings). Reports render at /admin/reports/matomo-reports (controller MatomoReportsController), the page-statistics block is plugin matomo_page_report, permissions are 'access matomo reports' and 'administer matomo reports'. Per the campaign brief, all medium/hard cases are grounded in this LOCAL config object - they never call the live Matomo API - so a passing case only proves the connection config was read/written correctly, not that a Matomo server responded.

evals.prompt: I installed matomo_reports on a Drupal 11 site. Where do I enter the Matomo server URL and the token_auth so reports show up, and how can different users use their own token instead of a shared one?
evals.expected_output: Go to Configuration > System > Matomo Reports (/admin/config/system/matomo-reports, route matomo_reports.matomo_reports_settings) and set the Matomo Server URL and (optionally) a global token_auth; these save to the matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings config object. If you leave the global token blank, each user with 'access matomo reports' can enter their own token_auth on their user-edit form (stored via the user.data service).

evals.prompt: Where do the Matomo analytics reports appear inside a Drupal site once matomo_reports is configured, and what permission does a user need to see them?
evals.expected_output: Under Reports at /admin/reports/matomo-reports (route matomo_reports.reports, controller MatomoReportsController), with tabs for visitors, actions, referrers, goals and transitions. A user needs the 'access matomo reports' permission.

evals.prompt: Does matomo_reports provide a block to show per-page view counts, and does it need any other module?
evals.expected_output: Yes - the 'Matomo page statistics' block (plugin id matomo_page_report). It requires the separate matomo (tracking) module because it reads the tracked site_id from matomo.settings; without it the block shows a prompt to install Matomo. Access is gated by 'access matomo reports'.

evals.prompt: This Drupal site already has matomo_reports pointed at a Matomo server. Inspect the live configuration and report the Matomo server URL it is configured to use.
evals.expected_output: matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings has matomo_server_url = https://matomo-known.example.com/matomo/ (read with `drush cget matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings`).

evals.prompt: On this site, matomo_reports restricts which Matomo sites users may view. Inspect the live configuration and state which Matomo site IDs are allowed.
evals.expected_output: matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings matomo_reports_allowed_sites = '2,5,9' (the comma-separated whitelist of Matomo site IDs).

evals.prompt: Configure matomo_reports on this site to talk to the Matomo server at https://analytics.mtask.example.com/matomo/ using the shared token_auth value 'anonymous'. Apply the change to the live site configuration.
evals.expected_output: In matomo_reports.matomoreportssettings set matomo_server_url = 'https://analytics.mtask.example.com/matomo/' and matomo_reports_token_auth = 'anonymous' (via the settings form or the config API).
